## Natural history notes

A medium-sized prominent moth characterized by mottled gray to brown forewings with angular dark lines, subtle pale patches, and a bark-like resting pattern that helps it blend against tree trunks and dead leaves. In Florida, the Angulose Prominent is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hardwood hammocks, pine-oak woods, forest edges, parks, and wooded yards where suitable hardwood host trees occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on tree foliage, especially oaks and related hardwoods, helping transfer leaf growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
